facts.raw_span: intractable mucocutaneous lesions that had been evolving for 10 years
No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes were palpable
Small bullae, erosions, and crusts were present on the lower lip
Erosions with epithelized mucosa were observed in the oral cavity
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions over erythematous and cicatricial lesions were present on the face, trunk, and extremities
Chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography showed no abnormalities
Gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy results identified no abnormalities
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis and superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
No obvious deposits of IgG, IgA, and C3 to either the epithelial cell surface or the basement membrane zone
Positive for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin (210 kDa) and periplakin (190 kDa)
Negative for Dsg1, Dsg3, and BP180 16th noncollagenous domain
Negative for BP230, type VII collagen, and desmocollins 1 to 3

concepts.why: The presence of mucocutaneous lesions, skin biopsy revealing spongiosis and superficial perivascular dermatitis, and positive IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin support this diagnosis.
The presence of flaccid bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin and mucous membranes is consistent with this diagnosis, although the negative results for Dsg1 and Dsg3 autoantibodies are unusual.
The presence of bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin is consistent with this diagnosis, although the negative results for BP180 and BP230 autoantibodies are unusual.

The presence of bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin, as well as the skin biopsy revealing superficial perivascular dermatitis, support this diagnosis, although the negative results for type VII collagen autoantibodies are unusual.
The presence of bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin is consistent with this diagnosis, although the negative results for IgA autoantibodies are unusual.

rationales.F01: Mucocutaneous lesions are common in several bullous diseases, but their intractable nature over 10 years may suggest a more complex condition like paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F08: The presence of spongiosis, neutrophils, and lymphocytic infiltration in the skin biopsy is highly suggestive of an autoimmune bullous disease, with paraneoplastic pemphigus being a strong candidate.
rationales.F10: The detection of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin is highly specific for paraneoplastic pemphigus, making it a strong rule-in finding for this condition.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, along with the clinical findings of intractable mucocutaneous lesions and the histopathological features, supports the diagnosis of Paraneoplastic pemphigus.
